stories.title: Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
stories.dek: The killings are the latest from a series of near daily attacks by Israel against what it says are Hamas targets.
stories.content:
Image source, Reuters Image caption, Dozens of Palestinians have been killed in Gaza in near daily air strikes over the past month

A Hamas political official and his wife were among eight Palestinians killed in three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday.

Local sources told the BBC a residential apartment in Deir al-Balah was targeted at dawn, killing Khaled Abu Nada - the deputy education minister - and his wife, Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada.

A Hamas Civil Defence spokesman said that rescue teams and medical personnel had transferred eight bodies to Al-Aqsa Hospital in central Gaza and Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.

In a joint statement, Israel's prime minister and defence minister said the operation was "part of a series of targeted killings" against Hamas officials.

Thursday's strikes also reportedly killed three Palestinians on al-Nafaq Street, east of Gaza City. Their identities have not yet been established, eyewitnesses said.

In a separate strike on Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, three Palestinians working for Hamas's security services were killed. They were identified as Yasser al-Lahham, Iyad Ahmed and Ibrahim al-Mashal.

Image source, @netanyahu/X Image caption, Khaled Abu Nada and his wife Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada were killed in the air strike

In a post X, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death of Khaled Abu Nada and said about 80 Hamas officials have been killed in the last month.

"No one in Hamas's leadership will succeed in evading us," he said, adding that the military would "continue to pursue our enemies and protect the security of Israeli civilians".

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had carried out a strike on a "senior" Hamas operative, and would provide further details later.

The attacks came a day after Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 47, the head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, his wife and their two teenage daughters were killed in Israeli air strike on their apartment in Shati refugee camp in Gaza City.

On Tuesday, the overall commander of Hamas's internal security service was among 10 Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes.

Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.

stories.dek: Five Israelis were also killed by the terrorists at Nariman House during the 2008 attacks

The 2008 attacks that continued until the morning of November 29 targeted several iconic locations bustling with people. File photo | Photo Credit: The Hindu

Israel on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said it stands firmly with India in the joint fight against terror as it honoured the memory of the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks.

"Today, Israel honours the resilience of the Indian people, the courage of those who risked their lives to protect others, and the memory of the innocent people murdered in the horrific 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks," Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs posted on X .

Today, Israel honors the resilience of the Indian people, the courage of those who risked their lives to protect others, and the memory of the innocent people murdered in the horrific 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. 🇮🇱🇮🇳 Terrorism knows no borders, and neither does our shared commitment to defeating it. Israel stands firmly with India in the joint fight against terror. @IndianDiplomacy @MEAIndia

On November 26, 2008, 10 heavily armed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists who sailed into Mumbai from Pakistan launched a gruesome coordinated terrorist attack on innocent citizens in the cosmopolitan city, leaving 166 people, including foreigners, dead and more than 300 injured, making it one of the deadliest terror strikes in an Indian city.

The Israeli Foreign Ministry said that terrorism knows no borders, and "neither does our shared commitment to defeating it."

Five Israelis were also killed by the terrorists at Nariman House.

"Israel stands firmly with India in the joint fight against terror," it said.

Read More : Execution of proclamation orders against Hafiz Saeed, five other 26/11 accused still awaited

The 2008 attacks that continued until the morning of November 29 targeted several iconic locations bustling with people, including the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Trident Hotel, Nariman House (Chabad House), Leopold Cafe and Cama and Albless Hospital.

stories.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
stories.dek: Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over past decade Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinia…
stories.content:
Palestinian prisoners in Ashkelon. More than three-quarters of respondents said they confessed after the use of torture. Photograph: Reuters View image in fullscreen Palestinian prisoners in Ashkelon. More than three-quarters of respondents said they confessed after the use of torture. Photograph: Reuters Israel Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over past decade

Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI).

This dangerous practice risked leading to irreversible miscarriages of justice, as Israel moved to implement a racist new death penalty law that targets Palestinians, the report said.

PCATI examined 42 cases in which Palestinians filed complaints about the use of torture by Shin Bet interrogators over the last decade.

More than three-quarters said they confessed after the use of “torture or other illegal methods”, and one in 10 provided incriminating statements about other people under torture.

“When it comes to Palestinian detainees, the Israeli legal system officially sanctions torture as a tool for extracting confessions, regardless of whether the content of those confessions is true,” said Sari Bashi, the executive director of PCATI.

“Torture as a tool of interrogation is particularly egregious given initiatives to impose the death penalty in Israel for the first time since 1962.”

Over the years, in hundreds of testimonies , Palestinian detainees have consistently described interrogations employing extreme sleep deprivation, physical violence such as slapping and kicking, threats, sexual violence and being held in stress positions.

Some of this abuse is also laid out in the official records of Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security service. PCATI details the case of a Palestinian lawyer arrested in February 2019 who was subjected to extreme sleep deprivation.

During an interrogation period lasting 27.5 days, or 660 hours, he was questioned for more than 552 hours, an average of 20 hours a day, with one session lasting nearly 48 hours. Some of the remaining 108 hours were spent travelling to and attending detention hearings.

In a 1999 ruling, Israel’s supreme court explicitly prohibited sleep deprivation as a deliberate interrogation method. Despite this, the lawyer was convicted of involvement in shooting attacks based on information extracted during this period.

stories.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
stories.dek: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows …
stories.content:
Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.﻿

Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.﻿

Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that’s designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come to market.

First spotted by Patentlyze , the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers.

According to the patent, My Channel would be able to churn out entire movies of various genres. If a user watches a lot of videos about Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , the system might serve up something like Ash Koosha’s Odysseus: The Fall . The patent details how My Channel might be able to connect to other streaming services — which would give it even more information about users and, presumably, access to useful training data for video generation. It all seems like a convoluted way to whip up AI knockoffs of professionally produced art, but what’s most unsettling about the patent are its mentions of My Channel creating digital avatars of users and turning them into “the protagonist or lead character” in the content it pumps out.

Setting aside the fact that My Channel would use photos, videos, and audio clips of people to create these avatars, the system sounds like it is designed to generate a form of “entertainment” that is deeply at odds with what makes engaging with art a worthwhile, enjoyable experience. It can be fun to metaphorically project one’s self into fictional narratives to understand how characters feel, but what Google is proposing is giving people access to an endless supply of bespoke content that doesn’t at all encourage them to use their imaginations to empathize with or relate to the characters. The patent makes it seem like Google thinks that viewers would be entertained enough just by seeing themselves onscreen. That’s bleak in and of itself because My Channel sounds very much like an unholy cross between JibJab and the panoptic elements of Google.

stories.title: Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists
stories.dek: Positrons are the antimatter counterpart of an electron.
stories.content:
Physicists at Northwestern University have achieved an unprecedented level of quantum control over a single positron, the antimatter counterpart of an electron. The breakthrough could eventually help scientists answer one of the most fundamental questions in physics: Why does the universe exist as we know it?

The researchers captured a rapidly moving positron produced through radioactive decay, slowed it down, and cooled it to a temperature just above absolute zero. They then confined the particle within a near-perfect vacuum, isolating it from ordinary matter, which would cause it to annihilate.

Using this approach, the team created what they call a "one-positron quantum cyclotron." Within this system, the positron behaves somewhat like an artificial atom, allowing researchers to observe and precisely manipulate its individual quantum energy levels.

The achievement lays the groundwork for what could become the most rigorous test yet of the fundamental symmetry between electrons and positrons. The Standard Model of particle physics predicts that the two particles should behave as nearly perfect mirror images of each other.

By measuring the positron's magnetic properties with unprecedented accuracy and comparing them with those of an electron, scientists could uncover previously undetected differences. Any unexpected discrepancy would point to a weakness in the Standard Model and potentially offer clues to why the universe contains so much more matter than antimatter.

"Antimatter gets its popular charm from science fiction," said Northwestern's Gerald Gabrielse, who led the study. "If you take an electron and an anti-electron (or positron) and collide them together, they both disappear. We describe that as annihilation, a concept that fuels science fiction writers' imaginations. The big mystery of the universe is the Big Bang should have created equal amounts of matter and antimatter. But, if that were true, it would annihilate, and we'd be left with nothing. There's clearly something wrong with that theory, and that's what we're trying to figure out."

Gabrielse is the Board of Trustees Professor of Physics at Northwestern's Weinberg College of Arts and Sciences and director of the university's Center for Fundamental Physics. Thomas Myers, a Ph.D. student working in Gabrielse's laboratory, is the study's first author.

The Standard Model is one of the most successful theories in modern science. It describes the universe's fundamental particles and three of its four fundamental forces (electromagnetic, strong nuclear and weak nuclear forces). Countless experiments have verified its predictions with remarkable accuracy.

stories.title: Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Agreements and Regional Energy Corridors
stories.dek: A multi-perspective assessment of offshore natural gas transit frameworks, maritime boundary negotiations, and regional stability.
stories.content:
The Eastern Mediterranean basin continues to navigate complex multilateral diplomatic engagements balancing offshore energy exploration with sovereign boundary delimitation. High-level delegations from regional coastal states and European partners are refining frameworks that align pipeline routes with equitable maritime economic zones.

Key Perspectives & Strategic Dimensions:
1. Energy Transit Security: Multilateral agreements between Mediterranean states prioritize uninterrupted transit of natural gas to Southern European ports, diversifying continental supply lines.
2. Maritime Boundary Delimitation: Diplomatic mediators emphasize that long-term maritime stability necessitates transparent dispute-resolution mechanisms that account for sovereign continental shelf claims.
3. Regional Economic Interdependence: Joint infrastructure investments in subsea interconnectors create economic mutual interest, offering pragmatic stabilization incentives across diverse stakeholders.
stories.whyItMatters: Directly impacts the economic stability, energy infrastructure, and security landscape across the Levant and Mediterranean.

stories.title: Sub-Microsecond Spin Dynamics in Diamond NV Centers: Benchmarking Cavity QED and Coherence Limits
stories.dek: Mitigating dipolar spin-spin dephasing and hyperfine bath interactions in dense diamond NV ensembles via Floquet driving.
stories.content:
Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond remain the preeminent solid-state platform for room-temperature quantum metrology and nanoscale magnetic resonance. Scaling from isolated defects to dense ensembles requires overcoming collective dephasing from the surrounding 13C nuclear spin bath.

Recent breakthroughs utilizing microwave cavity coupling and Floquet dynamical decoupling extend the effective coherence time (T2*) by an order of magnitude.

Key Technical Highlights:
1. Cooperative Purcell Enhancement: Dense NV ensembles entering the collective strong coupling regime demonstrate cavity-mediated coherence preservation.
2. Suppression of Spin-Diffusion Loss: Operating within crystallographic symmetry subspaces eliminates cross-axis relaxation.
3. Room-Temperature Sensing: Sustained microsecond coherence enables sub-picotesla magnetic field sensitivities for single-cell NMR.
stories.whyItMatters: Informs room-temperature diamond quantum magnetometry, microwave cavity loading, and advanced Floquet decoupling protocols in spin dynamics.

stories.source: Innatera & Edge AI Insights • 5 min read
stories.title: Sub-Milliwatt Neuromorphic Microcontrollers Shift Real-Time AI Inference to the Edge
stories.dek: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) on silicon processors achieve microsecond response times at sub-milliwatt power budgets.
stories.content:
The paradigm of routing sensor telemetry to centralized cloud servers is rapidly transitioning to on-device neuromorphic microcontrollers. Utilizing event-driven spiking neural architectures, silicon accelerators process acoustic and vibration patterns with near-zero latency.

Key Highlights:
1. In-Memory Processing: Spiking architectures circumvent the classical von Neumann memory bottleneck, consuming less than 1 mW.
2. Zero Cloud Exposure: Sensitive sensor streams remain strictly local, guaranteeing privacy and continuous operation during network blackouts.
3. Predictive Maintenance: Deployed microcontrollers classify industrial vibrations and structural stress in real time.
stories.whyItMatters: Enables zero-latency, private, on-device anomaly detection and vibration monitoring without cloud roundtrips.

stories.title: Circadian Photonic Priming and Equanimity in Demanding Research
stories.dek: Aligning 90-minute ultradian deep work blocks with natural circadian rhythms and secular Buddhist non-reactivity.
stories.content:
Sustained high-level analytical performance requires deliberate biological pacing. Structuring the day around 90-minute ultradian cycles followed by brief decompression intervals prevents cognitive fatigue.

Core Evidence-Based Habits:
1. Photonic Lock: Direct outdoor light exposure within 45 minutes of waking aligns the suprachiasmatic nucleus master clock.
2. Ultradian Block: Dedicate the primary 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM window to pure theoretical derivation before checking correspondence.
3. Secular Equanimity (Dhammapada 81): 'Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.'
stories.whyItMatters: Protects cognitive bandwidth and prevents attentional fragmentation during demanding laboratory derivations.

papers.title: Nitrogen-Vacancy Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy of $^{15}$N Spins in Potassium Nitrite Solution
papers.authors: Sehrish Iqbal, Jitender Kumar, Suvechhya Lamichhane et al.
papers.tldr: Nitrogen is essential in agricultural fertilizers, yet its nanoscale interfacial dynamics remain largely unexplored. Although quadrupolar broadening complicates $^{14}$N nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) detection, $^{15}$N (I=1/2) provides well-defined nuclear-spin signatures but remains challenging to detect at the nanoscale due to its low natural abundance and small gyromagnetic ratio.
takeaways: Although quadrupolar broadening complicates $^{14}$N nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) detection, $^{15}$N (I=1/2) provides well-defined nuclear-spin signatures but remains challenging to detect at the nanoscale due to its low natural abundance and small gyromagnetic ratio.

Here, we use a microfluidic quantum sensing platform based on shallow nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond to detect $^{15}$N NMR from KNO$_{3}$ solution at room temperature and in a low magnetic field regime.
This is consistent with the formation of a KNO$_{3}$ adsorption layer on the diamond surface, supported by surface characterization.

papers.title: Phonon-Aware Electron-to-Nuclear Spin Quantum Memory in NV Centers
papers.tldr: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a promising solid-state platform for quantum memory: the electron spin can be optically initialized and read out, while nearby nuclear spins have long coherence times and can serve as storage qubits. In this work, we develop a phonon-aware open quantum system model for electron-to-nuclear spin state transfer in a single NV center.
takeaways: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a promising solid-state platform for quantum memory: the electron spin can be optically initialized and read out, while nearby nuclear spins have long coherence times and can serve as storage qubits.
In this work, we develop a phonon-aware open quantum system model for electron-to-nuclear spin state transfer in a single NV center.

With the default decoherence rates, increasing the spin-phonon coupling from 0 to 0.06 MHz lowers the worst-case retrieval fidelity from 0.9994 to 0.9884, and the fidelity oscillates with the phonon-mode period because electron-phonon entanglement generated during the write step is partially undone during the read step.

papers.title: Infrared-absorption magnetometry in a diamond nanocavity: demonstration and limits at the nanoscale
papers.authors: Nicholas J. Sorensen, Elham Zohari, Chris Coutts et al.
papers.tldr: Diamond quantum sensors promise both high spatial resolution and high sensitivity; however, conventional photoluminescence-based spin readout can be difficult to integrate efficiently. Infrared absorption by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond provides a promising alternative, although the sensitivity of compact absorption-based sensors is limited by the short optical interaction length between the probe field and the NV ensemble.
takeaways: Diamond quantum sensors promise both high spatial resolution and high sensitivity; however, conventional photoluminescence-based spin readout can be difficult to integrate efficiently.

Infrared absorption by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond provides a promising alternative, although the sensitivity of compact absorption-based sensors is limited by the short optical interaction length between the probe field and the NV ensemble.
To overcome this limitation, we demonstrate, for the first time, singlet-absorption magnetometry using spin-dense diamond nanocavities.

papers.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
papers.tldr: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies. While accurate methods for spin dynamics are limited to relatively small systems, the dissipative spin environments in real experiments typically involve orders of magnitude more spins.
takeaways: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies.
We show that our method is applicable to systems containing arbitrary spin species under dynamical decoupling pulse sequences.

We demonstrate that cluster spin-LSC recovers numerically exact coherence and population dynamics for a nitrogen-vacancy center and a molecular qubit, reducing day-long multi-GPU simulations to only minutes on a CPU.

papers.title: Signatures of Kitaev quantum spin liquid states in $α$-RuCl$_3$ revealed by nitrogen-vacancy spin-noise spectroscopy
papers.authors: Jitender Kumar, Sehrish Iqbal, Himani Saraswat et al.
papers.tldr: Bond-dependent magnetic interactions, strong spin-orbit coupling, and quantum fluctuations in $α$-RuCl$_3$ make it an archetypical candidate for exotic Kitaev quantum spin liquid (QSL) states. While electronic transport, neutron scattering, optical and tunneling spectroscopies were used to probe global QSL signatures in large scale $α$-RuCl$_3$ samples, nanoscale evidence of local QSL behavior via a non-invasive experimental probe is still missing.
takeaways: Here, we use diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spin-noise spectroscopy to probe QSL states in α-RuCl3 nanoflakes with thicknesses ranging from 8 to 150 nm over a temperature range of 4.3-250 K.

Our measurements reveal a pronounced decrease in the NV spin-lattice relaxation time ($T_{1}$) below ~100 K in proximity to the $α$-RuCl$_3$ flakes, indicating enhanced GHz-frequency magnetic fluctuations.

These results establish NV spin-noise spectroscopy as a local, non-invasive probe of low-energy spin dynamics in $α$-RuCl$_3$ nanoflakes and open a route to testing predicted noise signatures of fractionalized excitations in atomically thin QSL candidates.
